rel-payment.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Payment / Financial system detected. This release likely has regulatory obligations. Ensure: DORA Article 9 change authorisation is documented; PCI-DSS scope is assessed if card data is involved; CAB approval is obtained before go-live; rollback and incident escalation paths are pre-agreed with your CISO and compliance team.

rel-auth.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Authentication / Identity change detected. Auth changes carry elevated risk — a failed deployment can lock out all users. Recommend: parallel auth path during deployment; blue-green or canary strategy; smoke test login flows as the very first post-deploy check; confirm rollback does not invalidate active sessions.

rel-db.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Database / Schema change detected. Data changes are typically the hardest to roll back. Require: pre-deployment snapshot; forward-and-backward-compatible migration (expand/contract pattern); DBA sign-off at the Pre-Prod gate; explicit rollback script tested in a non-production environment before go-live.

rel-emergency.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Emergency release pattern detected. Compressed gate process applies: Dev Complete → Go/No-Go → Deploy → Hypercare. All gate waivers require Director-level approval and must be documented. Post-implementation review is mandatory within 5 business days. ECAB (Emergency CAB) approval required in regulated environments.

rel-mobile.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Mobile delivery detected. App store review times: Apple ~1–3 business days, Google ~1–3 business days. Factor this lead time into your target date. A release date of less than 4 days from today is at risk if mobile is in scope.

rel-gdpr.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Personal data / GDPR scope detected. A DPIA (Data Protection Impact Assessment) review is required if this release changes how personal data is processed. Engage your DPO before the UAT gate. ICO breach notification within 72 hours applies if a release-related incident exposes personal data.

rel-thirdparty.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Third-party / supplier dependency detected. Confirm: the supplier has been notified and their change window aligns; contract SLAs cover the deployment window; you have a supplier escalation contact available on go-live day; dependency versions are pinned and tested.

rel-pilot.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Pilot / Limited release pattern detected. Ensure: pilot cohort is defined and consented; feature flag is tested on/off; exit criteria for full rollout are documented and agreed with product owner; telemetry is active to measure pilot outcomes; rollback = feature flag OFF (instant, no deployment required).

rel-decom.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Decommission / Sunset detected. Checklist: all consumers of the decommissioned service have been migrated; data retention obligations are met; audit logs are preserved; the decommission is reversible (or if not, a no-rollback decision is formally documented and approved); affected teams have been notified.

rel-S1-payment+auth.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Payment / Financial system detected. This release likely has regulatory obligations. Ensure: DORA Article 9 change authorisation is documented; PCI-DSS scope is assessed if card data is involved; CAB approval is obtained before go-live; rollback and incident escalation paths are pre-agreed with your CISO and compliance team.

rel-S2-4dm+payment.html:
⬡ Intelligence
High-complexity multi-model release. 4 delivery models selected. Releases spanning 4+ delivery models have statistically higher change failure rates. Consider: breaking into smaller releases where possible; assigning a dedicated contact per delivery model for the go-live window; extending the hypercare period to 72 hours minimum.

def-crash.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Critical failure pattern. This sounds like a release-blocking defect. Severity: Critical. Classification: Release Blocker. This must be resolved before go-live unless a formal Director-level waiver is documented with accepted risk.

def-payment.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Payment / financial impact detected. Any defect affecting payment flows is classified as a Release Blocker unless explicitly waived by the Head of Engineering and Risk. Regulatory reporting obligations may apply if this has already reached production.

def-login.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Authentication / access defect. Authentication failures typically classify as Release Blockers — a broken login prevents all user access. Confirm scope: is this all users, a subset, or a specific browser/device? Severity: High to Critical.

def-dataloss.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Data integrity defect. Data loss or corruption is always a Release Blocker. Additionally: notify your DPO if personal data is involved (UK GDPR 72-hour ICO notification may apply); check if a rollback of data is feasible; consider a data audit before re-deploying.

def-performance.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Performance defect detected. Performance issues are often deferred unless they breach SLA thresholds or cause user-facing errors. Assess: does this exceed the agreed response time SLA? Is it reproducible in pre-prod under load test conditions? If yes to either, consider reclassifying as a Blocker.

def-cosmetic.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Cosmetic defect detected. Cosmetic issues are typically classified as Known Issues and deferred to a future patch release. Confirm the defect does not affect accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA compliance) or create user confusion that could result in incorrect data entry.

def-browser.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Browser / device-specific defect. Assess the user population affected: if the failing browser/device accounts for >10% of your user base, this warrants High severity. Consider whether a Known Issue notice can be communicated to users while a fix is prepared.

def-security.html:
⬡ Intelligence
Security vulnerability detected. Security defects are always Release Blockers. Additionally: notify your CISO and security team immediately; assess whether the vulnerability is exploitable in the current state; DORA Article 17 and FCA SUP 15 may require regulatory notification if this is already in production.
